info.description: Offline fallback — live Init is patches/init.json

volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB, slider −120…0 dB with −18 dB at the middle). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

rate.tooltip: Steps per second. f replaces Rate; Adv takes priority over both.

steps1.tooltip: Kick ring length in steps. Each ring loops independently.

hits1.tooltip: Evenly distributed occupied steps on Kick. Values above Steps fill the ring.

rotate1.tooltip: Offsets Kick by this many steps, wrapping around its own length.

steps2.tooltip: Snare ring length in steps. Each ring loops independently.

hits2.tooltip: Evenly distributed occupied steps on Snare. Values above Steps fill the ring.

rotate2.tooltip: Offsets Snare by this many steps, wrapping around its own length.

steps3.tooltip: Hat ring length in steps. Each ring loops independently.

hits3.tooltip: Evenly distributed occupied steps on Hat. Values above Steps fill the ring.

rotate3.tooltip: Offsets Hat by this many steps, wrapping around its own length.

steps4.tooltip: Melody ring length in steps. Each ring loops independently.

hits4.tooltip: Evenly distributed occupied steps on Melody. Values above Steps fill the ring.

rotate4.tooltip: Offsets Melody by this many steps, wrapping around its own length.

drift.tooltip: Adds this rotation whenever each ring completes its own loop. Restart clears it.

reset.tooltip: Restart all rings after this many global advances. Zero disables automatic restart.

semitoneOffset.tooltip: Transposes the held Melody pitch from note number 57.

pitchRange.tooltip: Semitone span covered by the Melody position map.

pitchSource.tooltip: Classic uses a pentatonic map; Position uses the hit's normalized position directly. Both latch on Melody hits.

rate.tooltip: Clock rate in Hz. Wired ƒ cancels Rate (absolute Hz), same as oscillators.

pulseStart.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes high. Quantized to whole samples.

pulseEnd.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes low. Quantized to whole samples.

algorithm.tooltip: Hat design. 808: six PolyBLEP squares (205-800 Hz) through the 7.1 kHz band-pass and a high-pass. 606: six squares (606 tuning, by ear) into a resonant high-pass. FM: metallic FM carrier ring-modulated by a pulse pair, high-passed. Noise: band-passed white noise. Knobs keep their values when you switch.

tune.tooltip: Metal pitch scale, 1 = stock. 808 / 606: all six squares. FM: every operator. Noise: band-pass centre (8 kHz x Tune).

tone.tooltip: Brightness. 808 / 606: band-pass and high-pass move together, one octave down (0) to one up (1). FM: modulation index 2 -> 12 and high-pass. Noise: band-pass Q 0.5 -> 5.

closedDecay.tooltip: Closed hit decay: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60).

openDecay.tooltip: Open hit decay: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60).

metal.tooltip: Metallic source <-> white noise; 1 = all metal (stock 808 / 606). Noise algorithm: band-passed (1) <-> raw (0) noise.

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Does not scale Env.

algorithm.tooltip: Snare design. 808: two pinged resonators + high-passed noise. 909: two phase-reset rounded triangles + two noise bands. Simmons: SDS-V style sine with bend + resonant-lowpassed noise + click. FM: Chowning 1:1.4 FM drum + noise. Knobs keep their values when you switch.

tune.tooltip: Rest pitch of the body. 808: low resonator (high = x1.93). 909: VCO1 (VCO2 = x1.72). Simmons: oscillator. FM: carrier (modulator = x1.4).

tone.tooltip: Timbre. 808: low <-> high resonator mix (panel Tone). 909: noise lowpass 2 -> 12 kHz (brighter). Simmons: noise resonant lowpass 300 Hz -> 12 kHz. FM: peak FM index 0 -> 8.

snappy.tooltip: Snare-wire noise amount. 808: noise envelope level (panel Snappy). 909: level of both noise bands (panel Snappy). Simmons: noise <-> tone balance. FM: noise level.

bodyDecay.tooltip: How long the tonal body rings: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60). 808: low resonator (high 0.31x). 909: VCO1 envelope (VCO2 0.6x). Simmons: shared VCA (noise and tone). FM: carrier and FM index.

snapDecay.tooltip: How long the noise rings: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60). 808 / FM: noise envelope. 909: main noise band (this is the 909 panel's Tone). Simmons: extra noise envelope inside the VCA (at or above Body Decay = stock SDS-V).

bend.tooltip: Pitch drop at the hit: starts this many octaves above Tune and falls back. 0 = stock 808. 808 / 909 / FM: ~20 ms drop (909 ~0.5 oct). Simmons: falls over half the Body Decay (1-2 oct).

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Does not scale Env.

volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB, slider −120…0 dB with −18 dB at the middle). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

highFreq.tooltip: Sweep start frequency (the click). Latched on each Trigger. Clamped to 50 Hz ... half the sample rate.

lowFreq.tooltip: Frequency the sweep settles toward (a tuned body). 0 = keeps falling. Latched on each Trigger.

sweepTime.tooltip: Time to fall from High Freq to Low Freq + 50 Hz. Latched on each Trigger. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

chirp.tooltip: Tail power of the sweep. + holds the highs longer, then drops fast. - drops fast at first, then lingers low. Acts at once. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

chirpShape.tooltip: Attack knee vs decay at the same tail power. + keeps the start frequency a little longer, - rounds the knee. Acts at once. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

wave.tooltip: SawSine: fat saw (Morph 1) to sine (0). TriSine: hyperbolic tent, triangle (1) to sine (0). SawTri: saw (1) to triangle (0). Morph 1 is high-frequency content.

waveShape.tooltip: 1 = high-frequency end, 0 = low-frequency end. Modulate 1→0 as the kick falls. TriSine floors tent softness by pitch so the triangle end does not alias like a naive tent.

phase.tooltip: Start phase offset. Trigger hard-resets the oscillator to this phase. 0 = clean start at zero. +-0.25 = starts at a peak: hard click.

decay.tooltip: Amplitude envelope: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60) after a hit. Drives the 0–1 output and the Kick level. Acts at once.

amplitude.tooltip: Kick output level. Does not scale the 0–1 output.

voices.tooltip: How many stolen tails can fade at once. Only one kick is live; a retrigger fades the previous over Fade Time. Decay does not stretch Fade Time.

voiceFade.tooltip: On: a stolen voice fades out over Fade Time instead of cutting (no retrigger click, including Voices 1). Off: hard cut.

rate.tooltip: Master clock cycles per second. Zero pauses the internal clock; f or Clock overrides this control.

divide1.tooltip: Divider A's full gate cycle lasts this many master clock ticks. 1 follows the master clock.

offset1.tooltip: Shifts divider A by this many master clock ticks, wrapping within its own division. Positive values delay the pattern.

divide2.tooltip: Divider B's full gate cycle lasts this many master clock ticks. 1 follows the master clock.

offset2.tooltip: Shifts divider B by this many master clock ticks, wrapping within its own division. Positive values delay the pattern.

divide3.tooltip: Divider C's full gate cycle lasts this many master clock ticks. 1 follows the master clock.

offset3.tooltip: Shifts divider C by this many master clock ticks, wrapping within its own division. Positive values delay the pattern.

divide4.tooltip: Divider D's full gate cycle lasts this many master clock ticks. 1 follows the master clock.

offset4.tooltip: Shifts divider D by this many master clock ticks, wrapping within its own division. Positive values delay the pattern.

logic.tooltip: Combines gates before extracting triggers. OR: any gate high. XOR: an odd number high. AND: all four high. Logic changes can themselves produce an edge.

contrast.tooltip: Positive emphasizes stronger spectral regions; negative lifts weaker regions relative to the mean. Relative contrast is independent of input level. Zero disables contrast.

scale.tooltip: Spectral neighborhood width across 32 overlapping logarithmic analysis regions. Zero keeps regions independent; broad values link their dynamics. This is not FFT size.

thresholdDb.tooltip: Downward compression threshold for each stereo-linked analysis region, not whole-signal peak level. Ratio 1 disables threshold compression.

ratio.tooltip: Downward compression ratio above Threshold. One leaves the threshold stage neutral.

attackMs.tooltip: Gain-reduction time constant. Spectral gain decisions update every 256 samples; zero means one-hop response.

releaseMs.tooltip: Time constant for gain recovery and upward detail enhancement.

maxBoostDb.tooltip: Explicit maximum positive spectral gain before Output Gain. Prevents upward contrast from giving arbitrarily large boost to near-silent regions. This is a gain limit, not an audio clipper.

gainDb.tooltip: Output makeup gain after spectral processing. No hidden loudness normalization, saturation or limiter.

mix.tooltip: Dry/wet blend with both paths aligned to the fixed 1024-sample delay. Contrast 0, Ratio 1 and Output Gain 0 are neutral.

aa.tooltip: Antialiasing. Off is the raw clip. ADAA1 uses the previous sample. ADAA2 uses two previous samples and falls back when the input is flat.

drive.tooltip: Input push into the soft-knee curve.

threshold.tooltip: Amplitude (0...1) where limiting starts. Below this the driven signal is unchanged.

knee.tooltip: How gradual the transition from Threshold toward full scale is. 0 = hard at Threshold.
